# Network overview templates

Two parts: the true overview, `gm/network-overview.yaml` (part 1), and the
handout, `player/network-overview.md` (part 2), rendered from the same
entries (with a planted overview fault's change applied). Replace every
`<placeholder>`; a generated file keeps none. The loader checks both
(`tools/gm/model.py`, "the network overview"; capture W2 items 3 to 5 of
the v0.6 wave log).

## Part 1: `gm/network-overview.yaml`

```yaml
# gm/network-overview.yaml: the true network overview of <scenario-id> (sealed).
# Generated by the network-overview skill from the files generated_from: lists;
# never edit by hand: change an input and regenerate. It describes the system as
# designed, before any fault is planted (master spec 8.2, 8.4).
generated_from:                     # every input, its digest: sha256 of the file's bytes, in
                                    # model.overview_inputs' order, nothing else
  scenario.yaml: sha256:<hex>
  <nodes/records/postgresql.conf>: sha256:<hex>   # each customer node's seed files the fields
                                    # read (postgresql.conf, crontab, jobs.yaml, schedule.yaml,
                                    # api.yaml, exporter.conf, sources.yaml, health.yaml,
                                    # prometheus.yml) and its data file
  catalog/bricks/<postgres>/brick.yaml: sha256:<hex>   # each customer node's brick (the
                                    # scenario's bricks/<id>/ first, without catalog/)
  catalog/domains/<vet-core>/data/overview.yaml: sha256:<hex>   # each composed domain's
                                    # fragment, then its data/cron.sql when it has one
  catalog/purposes/<id>/purpose.yaml: sha256:<hex>   # each purposes: entry, then its ddl: files
  <player/partners.md>: sha256:<hex>   # when the bastion maps partners.md
  gm/data-register.yaml: sha256:<hex>  # when the scenario has a register
  gm/answer-key.yaml: sha256:<hex>     # with every overview_diff written
  player/story.md: sha256:<hex>
header:                             # master spec 8.1's fixed text, as rendered; never a deviation
  customer: <the customer's name: story.md's first "# " heading>
  network: One private network; the partners' services are reached on it by name; from outside,
    only the bastion's SSH port and web port are reachable.
  bastion: 'You work from `bastion`, your access point: [Node health](/grafana/d/node-health/node-health?var-node=bastion&from=now-6h&to=now).'
  node_health: 'Node health for the whole estate: [Node health](/grafana/d/node-health/node-health?from=now-6h&to=now).'
  trust: This is the centre's own documentation, kept by its IT. The **Your access** column is
    the game's rule and always exact.
entries:                            # one per customer node: 8.1's groups in order, each group in
                                    # scenario.yaml's order; never the bastion, never a third
                                    # party's node
  - node: <records>                 # the Docker name
    group: <database>               # database | application | integration | monitoring
    role: <database server>         # the skill's fixed table (SKILL.md, "Role")
    access: <write (`/etc/postgresql`)>   # 8.3's mapping, never a deviation
    activity: '[Node health](/grafana/d/node-health/node-health?var-node=<records>&from=now-6h&to=now)'   # 8.6
    description: <nodes[].description, one line>
    site: <nodes[].site>            # only when the node has one
    system: <Debian GNU/Linux 13>   # the brick's base:
    applications: <PostgreSQL 19; preloaded: pg_stat_statements, pg_cron; options: monitoring;
      report tools: pgbadger; cron>
    sizing: <CPU 1 (0.5 reserved), memory 1G (512M reserved), disk 2.25G>
    databases:                      # [] but on a database server (a standby: [])
      - database: <clinic>
        holds: <the medical record, the wards and the agenda>   # one line
        register: [<vet-core-owners>]   # the register's index for <node>/<database>; [] when none
    fed_and_used_by:                # [] but on a database server
      - node: <pms>                 # the connecting customer node
        database: <clinic>
        role: <vet_app>             # absent when the config names none (health.yaml)
        what: <the domain fragment's who; reads ...; writes ...>
    uses:                           # the same connections from the node's side, then HTTP
      - node: <records>
        database: <clinic>
        role: <vet_interfaces>
        what: <...>
      - node: <lab-api>             # an HTTP use of a customer API
        what: <the lab's order API: the centre's lab orders and their results>
      - partner: <Northfield Veterinary Laboratories>   # an HTTP use of a third party, by name
        what: <the send-outs and their results>
    users:                          # nodes[].users, as written; may be []
      - who: <the practice manager>
        database: <clinic>
        role: <vet_app>
    third_parties:                  # each partner the node reaches; may be []
      - partner: <Cold Storage>
        anchor: <cold-storage>      # its section of partners.md
        what: <the WAL archive and the nightly base backup>
    tasks:                          # each scheduled task on the node; may be []
      - task: <close-lab-statements>   # a job's name, a crontab entry's description, a pg_cron
                                    # job's name
        when: <0 4 1 * *>
        zone: <UTC>                 # UTC for jobs and crontabs; {{customer_timezone}} for pg_cron
        what: <one line>
        source: <jobs>              # jobs | crontab | pg_cron | purpose
    backups:                        # what protects the node's data, or the one item none
      - kind: <wal-archive>         # standby | wal-archive | base-backup | vault | check | none
        line: <WAL archived to Cold Storage, segment by segment>
third_parties:                      # one row per partner with a player_doc, access none
  - id: <cold-storage>
    name: <Cold Storage>
    hostname: <cold-storage>        # the hostname the players call
    anchor: <cold-storage>          # player_doc's fragment
```

## Part 2: `player/network-overview.md`

The handout, from the entries as the planted overview faults left them.
One line per fact, so a fault's change replaces whole lines of one entry.
Anchors follow GitHub's rule (lower-case; every character but letters,
digits, spaces, `-` and `_` dropped; spaces to `-`), as the bastion's page
renderer writes them (W2 item 2). Every field is written; an empty list
reads "none".

```markdown
# Network overview: <customer>

<network>

<bastion>

<node_health>

<trust>

## Summary

| Name | Role | Description | Your access |
|---|---|---|---|
| [<node>](#<node>) | <role> | <description> | <access> |

## Database servers

### <node>

- **Name**: `<node>` (`ssh <node>`, `psql -h <node>`)   <!-- `ssh <node>` alone off the database servers -->
- **Role**: <role>
- **Description**: <description>
- **Site**: <site>                  <!-- only when the entry has one -->
- **System**: <system>
- **Applications**: <applications>
- **Sizing**: <sizing>
- **Your access**: <access>
- **Activity**: <activity>
- **Databases**:
  - `<database>`: <holds>; register: [<entry id>](data-register.md#<its anchor>), ...
- **Fed and used by**:
  - `<node>`, database `<database>` as `<role>`: <what>
- **Uses**:
  - `<node>`, database `<database>` as `<role>`: <what>
  - `<api node>`: <what>
  - <partner name>: <what>
- **Users**:
  - <who> (database `<database>`, as `<role>`)
- **Third parties**:
  - [<partner>](partners.md#<anchor>): <what>
- **Background tasks**:
  - `<task>`, <when> (<zone>): <what>       <!-- a crontab entry: "<when> (<zone>): <what>" -->
- **Backups**:
  - <line>

## Applications and APIs

## Integration and back-office engines

## Monitoring

## Third parties

Each partner is reached by its hostname on the network; you have no access to its machines. What each offers is in [the partners' page](partners.md).

| Partner | Hostname | Your access |
|---|---|---|
| [<name>](partners.md#<anchor>) | `<hostname>` | none |
```
